title: When should you NOT use /grill-me?
summary: Matt Pocock presents a decision tree for choosing how much upfront alignment an agent task needs before any code is written. For a new piece of work, the first question is whether the resulting diff is really small: if yes, skip alignment entirely and just one-shot it, because a small change is cheap to redo if it is wrong. For medium-sized work, use a /grill-me session where the agent interviews you until you reach a shared understanding, which pays off by preventing a massive diff of stuff you did not want. If the grilling session starts expanding beyond what fits one conversation, switch to Wayfinder, which stretches planning across multiple sessions with a Wayfinder map and prototyping, letting you effectively grill at infinite scale for huge pieces of work or apps planned almost from scratch.
what_you_learn: You get a practical, three-way decision rule for a daily agent-workflow question: when to fire off a change with no planning, when to invest in an upfront specification interview with the agent, and when the scope is too big for one session and needs a multi-session planning method. The core insight is matching alignment effort to the cost of being wrong on the diff.

learnings.title: Start every new piece of agent work by sizing the diff
learnings.detail: When you open a new session and do not know which approach to choose, the first question is: is the resulting diff - the actual code change being created - really small? That single judgment is the root of the whole decision tree, because it determines the cost of getting the work wrong.

learnings.title: Really small changes should be one-shot, not grilled
learnings.detail: If the diff is really small, Matt recommends not using /grill-me at all - just one-shot it and let the agent make the change directly. Grilling exists to prevent massive unwanted diffs, and a tiny diff cannot become a massive one, so the upfront interview adds overhead without proportional payoff.

learnings.title: Grilling works by interviewing you into a shared understanding
learnings.detail: In a /grill-me session, the agent interviews you until both sides reach a shared understanding of what should be built. The time you invest there pays off because the resulting build is actually what you want, instead of a large diff containing a wrong interpretation of your request.

learnings.title: Small changes have a low cost of being wrong
learnings.detail: The economic argument for one-shotting: if the thing you are building is really small, there is very little cost in getting it wrong - you can simply say 'no, that was not right, do it better' and the agent redoes it. Cheap reversibility removes the need for expensive upfront alignment.

learnings.title: Escalate to Wayfinder when grilling outgrows one session
learnings.detail: Sometimes a grilling session grows beyond what you expected - the implications multiply and you realize you cannot cover it in a single session. That is the signal to switch to Wayfinder, a method for stretching the planning over multiple sessions instead of forcing everything into one conversation.

learnings.title: Wayfinder lets you grill at infinite scale
learnings.detail: Wayfinder turns extended planning into a Wayfinder map, supports loads of prototyping, and lets you essentially grill at infinite scale and size. Matt recommends it for a huge piece of work or a huge application you want to plan almost from scratch - work where even a long grilling session is not enough.

learnings.title: The full decision tree in one line
learnings.detail: The summary of the flowchart: if the diff is really small, just one-shot it; if it ends up bigger than one grilling session can cover, Wayfinder it. Alignment effort is a dial you set by scope - none for tiny work, interview for medium work, multi-session planning for large work.

key_points: The first question of any agent task is: how big will the diff be?
Really small change? Do not grill - just one-shot it.
Grilling pays off when a wrong interpretation would produce a massive unwanted diff.
A tiny change is cheap to redo, so alignment on it is wasted overhead.
When one grilling session cannot hold the scope, switch to Wayfinder.
Wayfinder stretches planning across sessions so you can grill at infinite scale.
